Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

chastity noun

also modesty (sexual), sexual virtue, purity, a woman’s honour

classical

Plaut. Amph. 840: sed pudīcitiam et pudōrem et sēdātum cupīdinem
Cic. Cat. 2.25: hinc pudīcitia, illinc stuprum (Lewis & Short)

pudīcitia, pudīcitiae f.

noun, first declension

chastity, sexual honour, modesty

From pudīcus. Worshipped at Rome as a goddess (Liv. 10.23, Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • castitās, castitātis f. — purity of body, chastity

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Leg. 2.29 (Lewis & Short); Tac. Agr. 4 (Lewis & Short)

    Rare but classical (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • Nōn ego illam mihi dōtem dūcō esse, quae dōs dīcitur, sed pudīcitiam et pudōrem et sēdātum cupīdinem

    I do not count as my dowry what is called a dowry, but chastity, modesty and desire kept in checkPlaut. Amph. 839–840

See also chaste, modest, debauchery, I’m ashamed.

SourcesLewis & Short: pudicitia · Lewis & Short: castitas

Plautus, Amphitruo 839–840.
